daily_brief: The day after Tuesday's US midterm elections, the political fallout continues to dominate headlines as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress in January, marking a significant rebuke of President Trump's administration [BBC, RFI, The Hindu]. Vice President JD Vance issued a striking public critique blaming the Iran war for Republican losses, widely seen as positioning for a 2028 presidential run [BBC]. In France, a major day of nationwide strikes brought hundreds of thousands to the streets demanding higher wages and better public services, with 70,000 police deployed amid concerns about potential violence [BBC, RFI, Al Jazeera]. Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong received a 10-year prison sentence under the national security law, adding to his existing detention and drawing international attention to Beijing's ongoing crackdown on dissent [BBC, Le Monde]. In Israel, coalition negotiations intensified as former military chief Gadi Eisenkot emerged as the frontrunner to form a government after an ultra-Orthodox party declined to recommend Prime Minister Netanyahu [The Hindu]. Meanwhile, European aviation authorities grappled with a third consecutive day of bomb threats affecting dozens of flights, all of which have so far proven to be hoaxes [BBC, ABC Australia, France 24].

top_stories.headline: Democrats Sweep US Midterms, Vance Breaks With Trump Over Iran War
bullets: Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, with gains in traditionally Republican states including Texas
Vice President JD Vance publicly blamed the Iran war for Republican losses in a 600-word statement on X, marking a sharp break from President Trump
Trump deflected from the election results at a press conference focused on his $400 million White House ballroom project, avoiding discussion of the defeat
The election produced historic firsts including the first Black woman governor, first Native American female governor, and first Muslim US senator

top_stories.headline: France Deploys 70,000 Police as Nationwide Strikes Bring Hundreds of Thousands to Streets
bullets: Five major unions launched coordinated strike action joining high school student protests that began in September over poor conditions
More than 250,000 protesters took to the streets by midday across nearly 70 towns and cities, with estimates of 500,000-700,000 expected nationwide
Demands include higher minimum wage, tax reforms, and improved public services amid cost of living concerns
Some unrest reported in Lyon with a car set alight, attributed to radical left-wing 'black bloc' groups

top_stories.headline: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Sentenced to 10 Years Under National Security Law
bullets: Wong, 30, was sentenced for 'colluding with foreign forces' under Hong Kong's 2020 national security law
Having already served six years in prison, he was due for release in January but will now remain imprisoned until 2036
Wong has been arrested multiple times since beginning his activism as a teenager and was once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement
Critics say the law has silenced dissent; authorities maintain it is needed for stability

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Detailed Wong's courtroom appearance and provided extensive background on his activism

top_stories.headline: Israel Coalition Talks: Eisenkot Emerges as Frontrunner After Ultra-Orthodox Party Abandons Netanyahu
bullets: Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot positioned to receive mandate to form government after October 27 election ended in deadlock
United Torah Judaism, a longtime Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to President Herzog
An Arab-led party endorsed Eisenkot, though he has not clarified whether he would accept Arab support for a coalition
President Herzog has until November 11 to decide whom to task with forming a government; Netanyahu remains caretaker PM

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Ran two articles emphasizing Netanyahu's weakening position and the significance of ultra-Orthodox abandonment

top_stories.headline: Bomb Threats Disrupt European Aviation for Third Consecutive Day
bullets: At least 25 flights affected Thursday including diversions of Aer Lingus, Ryanair, and Wizz Air aircraft across Italy, France, Poland, Bulgaria, Austria and Czech Republic
Italian fighter jets escorted a Finnair flight to Rome; an Aer Lingus Dublin-Rome flight diverted to a French air base
Threats came via email signed by 'Fighters of the Male State' claiming to target a 'feminist regime'
No explosives found on any affected flights; EU transport commissioner said unclear if incidents are linked

sources.framing_note: Detailed the threatening messages and their purported ideological motivation

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Provided comprehensive list of affected flights
